q: our 27 month old is terrified of the potty. Seems like he’s even holding in the pee to avoid using potty. Advice?
cx: Day 3 of Oh Crap; a bad day 1 turned a good start into fear.

q: But we’re back to square one after my mom gave him a pull up while babysitting.
cx: 3-year-old who pooped on the potty about seven times; the grandmother's pull-up undid it.

q: I’ve done everything. Charts, candy, a poop prize that sits on the shelf, etc. he starts preschool in August. He’s so smart. HELP!
cx: Same parent; preschool as the deadline.

q: we end up spending the entire day on and off the toilet interrupting meals, overtaking outings and sometimes even preventing us from doing things because he holds it and then needs it so urgently.
cx: Trained with Oh Crap in March; months of on-and-off poop refusal since.

q: Choosing which bathroom in the house, choosing toilet or the potty, we have done books, we have done videos on our phones, we’ve bribed him, we’ve tried not making a big deal of it at all and letting him take the lead. I am all out of ideas at this point.
cx: Same parent listing what was already tried.

q: What about the method would create this pattern ?
cx: Asking a commenter who blamed the Oh Crap method for the withholding.

q: It definitely feels like every day is all about poop and I feel like I’m starting to lose it hahaha 💩 what has my life become 🫣
cx: Same parent, a day later.

q: Some things that helped were: reducing pressure around it to eliminate the power struggle (“let’s try” and “ok we’ll try again in a bit” instead of “you need to poop” and sitting on the toilet for long periods etc)
cx: Update six weeks later: not resolved, but less extreme.

q: We stopped letting it rule our days and that’s helped everyone even though it’s still frustrating when it happens lol
cx: Same update; what turned it was backing off.

q:
The frustrating part is they listen at daycare. 

But I am at a loss. We have tried everything, time outs, taking things away they care about, trying to talk to them… etc. and everything is useless.
cx: Two toddlers, 2.5 and nearly 4, a week after a third baby came home.

q: I miss my sweet boys that listened and had respect for others!
cx: Same parent.

q: Ignoring doesn’t work. Incentivizing doesn’t work. Pulling out the big guns AKA his favorite snack and a TV show doesn’t work. We just have to sit there and listen to it.
cx: 21-month-old with sudden inconsolable tantrums of 30 minutes to an hour.

q: Sometimes my husband thinks this developmental stuff isn’t normal and that it’s only our kid.
cx: Same parent, relieved others have the same.

q: Am I just supposed to be watching the monitor like a hawk to see the second they start to stir? That just doesn’t seem feasible.
cx: Eight days of Oh Crap with 23-month-old twins who poop right before and after naps.

q: I’ve tried so hard to set boundaries, to teach her what is and isn’t acceptable and it just goes in one ear and out the other.
cx: Parent of a 3-year-old who destroys things; parent's own health is failing.

q: Me and my partner are so exhausted, and at a loss really on what to do at this point
cx: Same parent; bedtime 'a war zone every night'.

q: I feel like all day is me begging him to sit on the potty for very little results. We have veered way off course and I don't know how to get us back on track.

q: So hard to stay consistent when you don't know if you are even helping
cx: Same parent replying to a tip.

q: I'm definitely in a power struggle I don't want to be in.

q: I knew toilet training wouldn't be fun but this is killing me
cx: Same parent.

q: I don’t know if that’s the right move or if I’m stepping in too fast. I want him to learn how to figure things out, but he’s also still little

q: I am sorry, but the "pants off" method is not what I can handle right now. We have carpets.
